page: Google Cloud Platform z4d-highmem-48-highlssd is a storage-optimized virtual machine belonging to the z4d server family. It features 48 dedicated vCPUs built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. The system is equipped with 378.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 7.88 GB per vCPU. The storage subsystem utilizes NVMe SSD technology, and no graphics processing units are included in this instance configuration.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a high memory-to-vCPU allocation, positioning it as a robust option for workloads requiring substantial memory capacity alongside significant processing power. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent compute performance without the resource contention typical of shared-core environments. Qualitatively, the combination of dedicated x86_64 cores, high memory density, and NVMe SSD storage architecture makes it a cost-efficient choice for enterprise workloads that demand high-throughput data processing without the overhead of GPU accelerators.

The z4d-highmem-48-highlssd is engineered for memory-intensive and storage-optimized workloads. It is appropriate for hosting large-scale databases, executing complex data warehousing tasks, running enterprise resource planning systems, and managing memory-heavy analytics pipelines. The absence of hardware acceleration via GPUs limits its applicability for deep learning training, but its substantial memory footprint and dedicated compute resources make it a viable option for high-throughput transactional databases and memory-cached applications.
